core_obligations: The implications from the ring to the prime localisations and from those to the maximal localisations are immediate, the first from catenarity of localisations (proof lines 25769-25772).

For the converse, given primes p contained in q, choose a maximal ideal containing q and use the correspondence of chains under localisation to conclude that the ring is catenary (proof lines 25773-25779).

For universal catenarity, take a finite type ring map, choose a maximal ideal below a given prime, localise, get catenarity upstairs by finite type descent, and apply the first case (proof lines 25779-25788).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the catenary case to localisations at maximal ideals through the correspondence of chains (proof lines 25769-25779).
Handle universal catenarity by localising along a finite type map (proof lines 25779-25789).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that catenarity and, for Noetherian rings, universal catenarity can be tested after localising at all primes or merely at all maximal ideals (statement lines 25751-25767). The proof does not reprove the theory of dimension chains: it uses catenarity of localisations for one direction, reduces the other to the correspondence between chains of primes and chains after localising at a maximal ideal, and treats universal catenarity by pushing the property along a finite type ring map and invoking the first case (proof lines 25769-25789). The correspondence of chains is what makes the maximal-ideal test sufficient. H2.
